en: The Apadāna of the Elder Harītakadāyaka Ekavihārivagga 8 I gave a *harītaka* fruit to the Buddha, the Great Sage, who was free from all defilements. By that root of merit, I have attained the state of an Arhat. Having abandoned birth, old age, and death, I am now cooled and liberated. I have reached the end of suffering; there will be no further existence for me.
“Harītakī, āmalaka,
mango, jambu, and vibhītaka;
kola, bhallātaka, and billa— ”
I myself shall carry him away.
Having seen the sage who had gone to the mountain cave,
absorbed in meditation and delighting in jhāna;
To the peerless Great Sage, who was being oppressed by illness,
[he] took a myrobalan fruit.
I gave it to the Self-Existent One;
as soon as he had consumed the medicine,
his illness was immediately pacified.
The Buddha, whose distress has been abandoned,
expressed his appreciation for me:
“By this gift of medicine, [may there be well-being].”
And by the subsiding of disease.
Whether born as a god or a human,
or born in another state of existence;
"May you be happy in every respect,
and may no disease come upon you.
Having said this, the Sambuddha—
The self-become, unconquered,
the wise one, ascended into the sky like a king of swans in the air.
Since the myrobalan fruit was given to the Self-Existent Great Sage,
from this birth onwards, [I have been free from disease].
Sickness has not yet arisen for me.
This is my very last one;
my final existence is now unfolding.
The three knowledges have been realized;
the Buddha’s teaching has been accomplished.
Ninety-four aeons ago,
I gave medicine at that time;
I do not know a state of woe—
this is the fruit of that medicine.
The defilements have been burnt away by me;
I dwell free from taints.
Welcome indeed has come to me...
[as before] ...the Buddha’s teaching has been accomplished.
The four analytical insights...
[and so on] ...the Buddha’s teaching has been accomplished.
Thus indeed the venerable elder Harītakadāyaka spoke these verses.
This is the eighth legend of the elder Harītakadāyaka.
